'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2024 Kursk offensive]]
****The [[Armed Forces of Ukraine]] destroy a second bridge over the [[Seym (river)|Seym]] river in [[Zvannoye]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5y36rdreq1o (BBC News)]
**[[Belarusian involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] reports that nearly one third of the [[Armed Forces of Belarus|Belarusian Army]] has been deployed along the [[Belarus–Ukraine border]], in response to [[Ukraine]] stationing more than 120,000 troops at the border. However, Ukraine claims no movement of Belarusian troops has been observed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-lukashenko-says-nearly-third-army-sent-ukraine-border-belta-reports-2024-08-18/ (Reuters)]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***The [[Russia]]n [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Ministry of Defence]] claims that [[Russian forces]] have captured the village of Svyrydonivka in [[Donetsk Oblast]], Ukraine. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/russian-forces-continue-to-advance-in-eastern-ukraines-donetsk-region-claiming-another-settlement/3307131 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Libyan crisis (2011–present)|Libyan crisis]]
**The [[Central Bank of Libya]] suspends all operations following the [[kidnapping]] of the head of its [[information technology]] department by an unknown party. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/libyas-central-bank-suspends-operations-after-kidnapping-official-2024-08-18/ (Reuters)]
*A [[bomb]] explodes in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]], killing one person and injuring another. [https://news.sky.com/story/one-dead-after-bomb-explodes-in-tel-aviv-israeli-police-say-13199528 (''Sky News'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 European floods]]
**Record rainfall strikes regions of the [[Austria|Austrian]] capital of [[Vienna]] with most of the city's average total summer rainfall falling in just one hour, causing significant [[Flood|flooding]] and damage throughout the city. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/austria-battles-major-flooding-after-record-downpours-2024-08-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Lebanese blackout]]
**Ongoing [[Power outage|nationwide blackouts]] in [[Lebanon]] caused by [[Energy crisis|fuel shortages]] provoke significant governmental conflict, with the [[Ministry of Energy and Water (Lebanon)|Minister of Energy]] blaming the [[Banque du Liban|Central Bank]] for not paying [[Iraq]] for fuel imports and the Central Bank blaming [[Parliament of Lebanon|Parliament]] for not authorizing [[emergency fund]] transfers for fuel payments. [https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5051732-lebanon-plunges-complete-darkness-gas-oil-runs-out-fuel-power-plants (Asharq Al-Awsat)]
*[[2024 Yemen floods]]
**More than 100 people are killed during nearly three weeks of persistent heavy rainfall and flooding across [[Yemen]], with the country's national weather agency declaring a [[Severe weather|severe weather alert]] for future "very heavy [[thunderstorm]]s". [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2567903/middle-east (Arab News)]
*At least eight family members are killed when their [[van]] collides with a [[delivery truck]] in [[Sariaya, Quezon]], [[Philippines]]. [https://qa.philstar.com/nation/2024/08/19/2378903/8-die-van-truck-collide-quezon-province (''The Philippine Star'')] [https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20240818/ccff3cedad5c4f309aaf5fe09389926c/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*An [[oil spill]] originating from the [[Carabobo#El Palito Refinery|El Palito refinery]] in [[Puerto Cabello]], [[Venezuela]], is reported to have contaminated more than {{conv|225|km2|mi2|abbr=on}} of the [[Gulf of Paria]] as well as most of [[Morrocoy National Park]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/oil-spill-reported-off-venezuelas-caribbean-coast-2024-08-17/ (Reuters)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Kidnapping in Nigeria]]
**Twenty medical students from the [[University of Jos]] and the [[University of Maiduguri]] are kidnapped while traveling in [[Benue State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/8/18/nigeria-police-working-to-secure-release-of-20-kidnapped-medical-students (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]]
**[[2024 Venezuelan protests]]
***[[Venezuelan opposition]] officials and supporters gather in cities across [[Venezuela|the country]] to protest against [[President of Venezuela|President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] and the results of the 2024 presidential election. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelan-opposition-protests-election-dispute-drags-2024-08-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[China–Vietnam relations]]
**[[President of Vietnam]] and [[General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam]] [[Tô Lâm]] arrives in [[China]] for a three-day state visit, Tô's first overseas visit since becoming president and general secretary. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/china-vietnam-lam-xi-jinping-market-economy-diplomacy-analysis-4554376 (CNA)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024 UCI Women's World Tour]]
**In [[cycle sport|cycling]], [[Katarzyna Niewiadoma]] wins the [[2024 Tour de France Femmes]] by four seconds, her first win at the event after placing third at the [[2022 Tour de France Femmes|2022]] and [[2023 Tour de France Femmes|2023]] events. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/18/sport/kasia-niewiadoma-tour-de-france-femmes-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
